newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL- BULLS BACKUP CENTER WENNINGTON OUT FOR THE PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL- BULLS BACKUP CENTER WENNINGTON OUT FOR THE PLAYOFFS.

text.p: The banged up Chicago Bulls will be without reserve centre Bill Wennington for the playoffs as his team attempts to repeat as National Basketball Association champions.

Wennington was injured in a March 29 game and missed the final 11 games of the season with a torn tendon in his left foot. The team announced Tuesday that it had elected not to put him on the post-season roster.

Wennington averaged 4.6 points and 2.1 rebounds in 61 games for the Bulls this season. He served as backup to Australian centre Luc Longley on last year's 72-win championship team. This season, he shared backup duties with veteran Robert Parish.
The Bulls expect ailing six-time rebounding champion Dennis Rodman and forward Toni Kukoc to be ready for the first round playoff series against the Washington Bullets.

Rodman has been bothered by a sprained knee ligament he suffered in the closing seconds of a March 25 home victory over the Dallas Mavericks. He sat out the final 13 games of the regular season nursing the injury.
The 35-year-old Rodman, who also missed 14 games due to spensions, again led the league in rebounding this season, pulling down 16.1 boards per game.
Kukoc, who missed 25 games this year with a torn foot tendon, averaged 13.2 points and 4.5 assists in 57 games.
Despite the injuries, the Michael Jordan-led Bulls again posted the best record in the NBA at 69-13 and own homecourt advantage throughout the playoffs.
The Bulls begin their title defence Friday when their best-of-five Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against Washington opens in Chicago.
